beats.title: Keep the crust soft for the rise
beats.outcome: Make a reasoned choice and name the evidence that would change it.
beats.explanation: [[hearth-m03-concept|Oven spring]] happens in the first minutes of baking, while the crust can still stretch. Steam keeps the surface moist for those minutes; without it the crust sets early and the loaf tears.

handbook.markdown: A covered pot traps the loaf's own steam. An open bake needs added steam. Either way the goal is the same: a flexible surface until the rise is done. The dough still needs [enough strength](#/module/hearth-m02) to hold that rise.

beats.recap: Oven spring happens in the first minutes of baking, while the crust can still stretch.

beats.title: Release steam to brown the crust
beats.outcome: Make a reasoned choice and name the evidence that would change it.
beats.explanation: Once the rise is done, the crust needs dry heat to brown. Release the steam by uncovering the pot, then finish the bake dry. A well-risen but pale loaf usually kept its steam too long.

handbook.markdown: Change the lid-off time in small steps and compare loaves from the same dough. Colour also depends on oven temperature, so change one factor at a time.

beats.recap: Once the rise is done, the crust needs dry heat to brown.
